docs.text: Open-source embedded software Kokeb Labs ¶ Open, brand-free drivers, firmware building blocks and tools for embedded systems. Every chip driver works on any MCU through a small port you write, builds and tests on a laptop, and ships with documentation and CI. Everything is MIT licensed. Browse the projects How we build GitHub From your firmware to the chip Figure description and sources Top to bottom, each arrow is a call. Your firmware calls the kb-core handlers, which call chip drivers (driver- ), which reach the hardware only through an MCU port, yours or a ready one from kb-core; the port drives the chip on your board. Dashed cards are planned. On the right, the tools that every repository uses: driver-template starts a driver, espidf-tools builds and flashes ESP-IDF projects, ci-tools checks, documents and releases them all. docs.text: Contributing ¶ Fork the repository and create a branch. Make your change; keep the docs and tests in the same pull request. Sign off every commit: git commit -s . CI fails a pull request with a commit that has no matching Signed-off-by: line. Open a pull request. CI gate runs every check; a maintainer reviews. The full guide, the code of conduct and the security policy are in the organisation's community files . Report a vulnerability privately through the repository's Security tab, never in a public issue.

docs.text: How we build ¶ Brand-free drivers ¶ A driver is named after its chip, not after a product: repository driver-<chip> , namespace <chip>:: . It never calls an MCU SDK. It calls a few hooks (transfer, GPIO, delay) on a port class you write, checked at compile time with no virtual calls, so the same driver runs on ESP-IDF, STM32, Zephyr, Linux and on the host for tests. Three kinds of "specific" ¶ Kind Example Where it lives Chip-specific the registers of one sensor in that chip's driver MCU-specific an ESP-IDF SPI port under interfaces/mcu/<family>/ , built only for that family Product-specific one product's pin map or modes never in a shared repository; products use extension points Every repository, the same checks ¶ A strict documentation build, figure and generated-table drift checks, link checks. C++ builds and host tests, clang-tidy and cppcheck over the same compile database. A DCO sign-off on every commit, an MIT licence and the required root files. One required check, CI gate , and every third-party action pinned to a commit SHA. Licence and sign-off ¶ Everything is MIT licensed, Copyright (c) 2026 The Kokeb Labs Authors . There is no CLA: you sign off each commit ( git commit -s ) to certify the Developer Certificate of Origin .

docs.text: Roadmap ¶ Foundations (done). The organisation, ci-tools v1, espidf-tools v1, driver-template , this site. Drivers. Chip drivers move in from HardFOC, renamed driver-<chip> , each with host tests and an ESP32 example. kb-core. One repository with kb::utils , kb::rtos , kb::interfaces and kb::handlers . Hardware abstraction. MCU ports under interfaces/mcu/<family>/ , starting with ESP32. HardFOC on Kokeb. The HardFOC boards build on these drivers and kb-core. Tools for users. A command-line tool, a board configurator and a documentation hub.
